claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy is single-phase BCC.
The initial TiVNbTa alloy has a dendritic microstructure.
Unmodified TiVNbTa has a yield strength of approximately 330 MPa at 1273 K.
Unmodified TiVNbTa has a compressive strength of approximately 423 MPa at 1273 K and 30% strain.
Fine oxide nanoparticles such as Y2O3 can be introduced into TiVNbTa as a controlled dispersion.
The introduced oxide nanoparticles will remain thermally stable at 1273 K.
The intervention will produce a relatively uniform dispersion of oxide nanoparticles in the TiVNbTa matrix.
Dispersed oxide nanoparticles will pin dislocations in TiVNbTa at elevated temperature.
Dispersed oxide nanoparticles will pin grain boundaries and suppress grain-boundary sliding at elevated temperature.
Dislocation and grain-boundary pinning will stabilize the TiVNbTa microstructure and reduce strength degradation at 1273 K.
Oxide dispersion strengthening will increase the yield strength of TiVNbTa at 1273 K relative to the unmodified baseline.
Oxide dispersion strengthening will increase the compressive strength of TiVNbTa at 1273 K and up to 30% strain relative to the unmodified baseline.
Testing at 1273 K under compression to 30% strain represents operating conditions relevant to a TiVNbTa interlayer between tungsten and CuCrZr.
